title: EVERSE Research Software (RS) Tools Validation Schema
description: Schema for validating software tool entries in the EVERSE Research Software context.

@id.description: Identifier for the quality dimension. Valid values are dynamically fetched from the EVERSE indicators API at validation time.

qualityDimensionObject.comment: The enum of valid dimension values is populated dynamically by helpers.py EVERSE api

@id.description: Identifier for the quality indicator. Valid values are dynamically fetched from the EVERSE indicators API at validation time.

qualityIndicatorObject.comment: The enum of valid indicator URIs is populated dynamically by helpers.py. If unavailable, validation is skipped.

keyword.description: A term from the TechRadar keyword list, describing what the tool does. To add a term, append an entry here with a one-line description and justify it in the pull request (see CONTRIBUTING.md).

oneOf.description: Checks source code or configuration files against style and correctness rules.
Rewrites source code to a consistent layout.
Analyses source code without running it, e.g. to find bugs or dead code.
Analyses a program while it runs, e.g. to find memory or threading errors.
Computes measures of the code such as complexity, size or duplication.
Looks for vulnerabilities, leaked secrets or insecure configuration.
Provides a way to write, organise and run automated tests.
Measures which parts of the code the tests execute.
Measures run time, memory use or other resources of a program.
Builds and tests code automatically on every change.
Runs checks automatically at Git events such as commit or push.
Proposes updates of a project's dependencies automatically.
Automates compiling and assembling software from source.
Installs and resolves dependencies and manages software environments.
Packages software with its dependencies into portable containers.
Deploys, scales and manages containers across machines.
Distributes software packages through a public index or registry.
Records the history of changes to source code.
Records versions of data and models alongside code.
Preserves software long term and assigns persistent identifiers (DOI, SWHID).
Builds documentation from source code or text files.
Creates, extracts or synchronises machine-readable software metadata (e.g. CodeMeta).
Helps make software citable, e.g. with CITATION.cff files.
Helps choose, declare or check licenses and copyright.
Evaluates software or data against the FAIR principles.
Evaluates software against a set of quality indicators or checks.
Gives written recommendations or guidance rather than running checks.
Generates a new project from a template that follows good practices.
Provides notebooks that mix code, results and text.
Uses AI models to suggest, write or review code.

@context.description: The JSON-LD context for term definitions

@id.description: Unique identifier for the software tool

@type.description: The type of the entity, typically schema:SoftwareApplication

name.description: The name of the software tool

description.description: A description of the software tool

identifier.description: An identifier for the software tool

isAccessibleForFree.description: Whether the software is free to access

license.description: License under which the software is released

hasQualityDimension.description: Quality dimensions addressed by the tool

measuresQualityIndicator.description: Quality indicators measured by the tool

improvesQualityIndicator.description: Quality indicators improved by the tool

howToUse.description: How the software is expected to be used

appliesToProgrammingLanguage.description: Programming languages the tool applies to

keywords.description: What the tool does, as terms from the TechRadar keyword list (definitions/keyword)
